svg.text: ZONE ADAPTATIONS — ONE DESIGN FAMILY, THREE HAZARD PROFILES
The tank does not change. What changes is where it sits, what it is sealed with, and what the overflow is for.
A — COASTAL BELT
Zones A & B · Khulna, Satkhira, Cox's Bazar
Cyclone wind · storm surge · salinity intrusion
Tank sealed and anchored: 4 × M16 SS anchors, tie-down
straps over the cover.
All fixings stainless 304. Galvanised steel corrodes to
failure in 3–4 years in salt air.
Epoxy lining mandatory: protects stored water from
chloride ingress through micro-cracks.
Plinth raised 300 mm above surrounding ground; site on
the highest point of the homestead.
MAR recharge pit is not optional here. It holds back the
freshwater lens that salinity is eating.
Emergency reserve valve: 14 days of drinking water sealed
in the tank before landfall.
TANK
M16 SS anchors + straps
storm surge level
Plinth on high ground, sealed cover, tied down
B — FLOOD PLAIN & HAOR
Zone C · Kurigram, Gaibandha, Sirajganj, Sunamganj
Annual monsoon inundation · flash flood
Tank on a raised plinth to at least 0.5 m above the
recorded 100-year flood level, from the BWDB gauge.
Anti-buoyancy: an empty tank in 1 m of floodwater has an
uplift 2.5× its own weight. It will float and tip.
If it cannot be raised, anchor to a mass concrete base of
at least 1.5× the uplift force.
Backwater flap valve on the overflow so flood water
cannot enter the tank.
Pre-flood protocol: fill the tank before the crest
arrives. A full tank is an emergency water point.
Keep the draw-off and tapstand 600 mm above the 100-year
flood level so it stays reachable.
100-yr flood level
TANK
mass concrete anchor if the plinth cannot be raised
uplift on empty tank
C — BARIND & CHAR
Zone D · Rajshahi, Chapainawabganj, Naogaon, char lands
Drought · low rainfall · arsenic in groundwater
Rainfall here is 1,157 mm in a dry year. Roof area is the
binding constraint — extend the catchment.
30 m² minimum catchment, not 20 m². Use a lean-to
extension or a separate sheet catchment if needed.
Tank sized at 5,000 L even though the roof rarely fills
it: the constraint is the dry season, not the monsoon.
MAR recharge is the primary benefit in a drought year —
it keeps the shallow aquifer alive.
RWH is the arsenic-free source. Never blend with tubewell
water that has not been tested.
Two tanks in series where the household can afford it:
decanting lets sediment settle in the first.
EXTENDED CATCHMENT 30 m²
TANK
MAR pit
Roof is the constraint, not the tank

Deployment rule: one standard design, three site adaptations. Never deploy the coastal anchorage detail in the Barind (wasted cost), and never deploy the Barind 20 m² catchment in Satkhira (it will not fill).
D-06 ZONE ADAPTATIONS
BORSHA-BANDHU INTEGRATED RWH SYSTEM
